$comment: MedAgentPro - Phase B, item B1. JSON schemas for every model call. Five schemas total. The domain interpretation schema is not here: it is already written and verified as Prompt B in section 3.3.1 of the book, 25 of 25.
book_version: Book_Phase_A 4.10, with chapter 8 added. References [1] to [43].

status_legend.blocked: cannot be written until the blocker is resolved
status_legend.demo: written against the demo store only; not in the book

placeholders.book: Table 15, readings a question may carry
not in Table 15. A prompt-width value with no reader-facing effect
not in Table 15. Equal to compiler.ROW_LIMIT, the most identifiers one reading presents (task 3, H7); checked in a test

intent_analysis.stage: Intent analysis and routing, query assistance pipeline only (Table 12).
compiler_checks: Every col resolves in schema.json, and its table is the FROM table or reached by a JOIN.
Every rel exists in relations.json and connects a table already in scope.

value type matches the column type it is compared against; both sides of a column-to-column comparison share a type. This is also what rejects a date or numeric column compared to an empty string, which would otherwise compile and return no rows for every question about an absent value.
IS_NULL and IS_NOT_NULL apply only to a column of the FROM table, never to a column reached through a JOIN.

GROUP_BY present if and only if SELECT mixes an aggregate with a non-aggregate field, and then it names every non-aggregate alias and no aggregate one. A SELECT of aggregates only carries no GROUP_BY, so a total count can be asked.
HAVING agg names an alias whose expr is a func. ORDER_BY by names an existing alias.
Aliases unique within a plan; label unique across readings.
Entitlement condition injected into WHERE per NFR 17, read from schema.json per role. A role absent from an entity grants no access.

LIMIT injected where omitted, at the same configured value that bounds it in this schema (Table 15, rows a retrieval returns). A count of the rows before LIMIT is taken in code, so a cut result is presented as a number of a total.
Every unresolved.asked overlaps the question text as posed. A span the question does not contain is rejected.

unresolved.needs carries an entity for every kind except unspecified, which must carry none. For no_such_column and value_not_present the entity resolves in schema.json. For no_such_table and source_outside_system it must not, since the gap states that the schema does not hold it.
Every metric name is declared in schema.json. The compiler expands it to its column expression; the model never writes that expression.
Every ambiguous.term overlaps the question text as posed, and every alternative resolves in schema.json.
Where ambiguous is non-empty, the number of readings is at least the number of alternatives declared for any one term. A declared ambiguity that produced a single reading is rejected.

Every value compared with a column marked identifier in schema.json appears in the question as posed, in an earlier question or answer of the conversation, or among the identifiers presented in an earlier answer (NFR 27, Test 45). The rewritten question is not a source, since the model wrote it, and neither is a summary of reduced exchanges. Matching is by whole token, so S-03 is not found inside S-031. Values of other columns are not checked: a period or a quantity is an interpretation of what was said.

disposition.$comment: FR 14. A question that requires attributing a cause or judging whether a value is anomalous is referred to an investigation instead of being answered. Deciding this here means no retrieval is planned for such a question. [demo extension, task 8 A1] out_of_scope_action: a request to change records rather than read them. Nothing is retrieved, and code answers with a fixed sentence. [demo extension, chat 18.10 11:35] needs_clarification: a question that cannot be interpreted from its own words and the conversation, such as a follow-up at the start of one. Nothing is retrieved, and code asks for the question in full with a fixed sentence. A term with more than one reading is not this: it is declared in ambiguous.

readings.$comment: FR 11. A question carrying more than one reading is presented under each of them rather than resolved. FR 16 executes them together. PLACEHOLDER: maxItems.

asked.$comment: A span of the question as the person posed it, not a restatement. Verified in code against the question text and rejected otherwise, so this field cannot carry an explanation or a cause (NFR 20).

unresolved.$comment: FR 11, second half. A part of the question no reading covers. asked points at the person's own words; needs names a kind of absence and an entity. Neither can carry a cause (NFR 20).

ambiguous.$comment: Terms in the question that more than one element of schema.json could express, with the alternatives considered. Declared in the same call, so it costs no additional model call. Each alternative is resolved against schema.json in code. An entry here is what makes a question carry more than one reading under FR 11.

term.$comment: A span of the question as the person posed it. Verified in code against the question text.

qualified.$comment: table.column. One store only, so a single qualifier is enough.

asked.$comment: [proposal, not in the book] Task 4, A (91_COVERAGE_PLAN, chat 20.10, 22:30): the span of the question this reading answers, in the person's own words, as unresolved[].asked. Verified in code as a span of the question; the spans of the readings and of unresolved together must hold every content word of the question (compiler.uncovered).

reading.$comment: label is the namespace for references produced downstream. A value drawn from this reading is carried as label.alias (NFR 6).

GROUP_BY.$comment: Names SELECT aliases, not expressions. The compiler expands each to its underlying column.

HAVING.$comment: Flat list, implicitly ANDed. agg names a SELECT alias whose expr is a func.

ORDER_BY.$comment: Orders by SELECT alias. NFR 6 rejects a reference that contradicts an ordering the retrieval stage determined, which requires the ordering to be over named output fields.

LIMIT.$comment: PLACEHOLDER: maximum. In query assistance there is no summarization stage (Table 12), so retrieved rows enter the synthesis prompt as held. Test 13 rejects a value outside this range, so the bound belongs here and not in the compiler.

plan.$comment: A stated subset of SQL grammar (3.1.6, Table 7). Not expressible: subqueries, UNION, CTE, window functions, AVG, OFFSET, DISTINCT, LIKE, raw SQL of any kind.

select_item.$comment: as is mandatory. It is the field name in the returned row and therefore the second half of every reference downstream.

join.$comment: rel names a relation declared in relations.json. The model never writes a join condition. Source [20] places schema linking at 29-49 percent of errors and join errors at 21-26 percent.

value.$comment: null is excluded as a literal. EQ against NULL is always false, so absence is tested with IS_NULL and IS_NOT_NULL rather than by comparing to a literal.

me.$comment: [demo extension, fix round D7] The person asking: "my", "mine", "I". The compiler fills the asker's user_id as a parameter; the model never writes it. Allowed only in EQ or NE against a column marked user_column in schema.json.

func.$comment: Counts, sums, averages, lowest and highest come from the store, not the model: computed in SQL, so each is a field of a retrieved row and is carried as a reference like any other. AVG is rounded to two decimals in code (chat, 18.10, 13:05; NFR 6 read as extended). It was excluded before, as existing in no row; computed in the query, it is a row of the result like COUNT. SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX also take a numeric metric (chat, 18.10, 13:15): rule 4 sends the model to the metric, so it must be possible to aggregate it. A boolean metric is counted with COUNT and WHERE, never aggregated (type_mismatch, in the compiler).

IN.$comment: [15.10] An object, not a tuple: Anthropic's structured outputs do not enforce prefixItems, and LiteLLM 1.105 drops prefixItems but keeps items: false, which leaves an array that must be empty. An object with every field required is enforceable without prefixItems, which Anthropic does not support (00_STATUS, task 10a, chat 01:40).

BETWEEN.$comment: [15.10] An object, not a tuple: Anthropic's structured outputs do not enforce prefixItems, and LiteLLM 1.105 drops prefixItems but keeps items: false, which leaves an array that must be empty. An object with every field required is enforceable without prefixItems, which Anthropic does not support (00_STATUS, task 10a, chat 01:40). Both ends included, as SQL BETWEEN.

MATCHES.$comment: [proposal, not in the book; chat 20.10, V7] A name the user wrote, passed as written. Only on a column schema.json marks searchable, anywhere in WHERE, a positive condition (V1 relaxed in task 3, 40_CHAT section 17: a name resolved to one entity becomes EQ on its identifier, under OR too; one not resolved stops the whole reading); term is a span of the question. Resolved in code against the entity's identifier, within the user's entitlement (81_VALUE_MATCH). An object, not a tuple.

oneOf.$comment: Unary. Tests for an absent value. Restricted by the compiler to a column of the FROM table, so that IS_NULL combined with a LEFT JOIN cannot be used as an anti-join.

IN_READING.$comment: [proposal, not in the book; task 3, 92_TASK3_PLAN, chat 21.10 12:50] The record's col equals the value of alias as in some row of the reading named. col and the column behind as must identify the same entity (its identifier, or a column that declares references to it), checked in code. reading is another reading of the same plan that holds no reference itself (depth 1); only under AND from the root of WHERE. Compiled to EXISTS over that reading's own query, entitlement included. An object, not a tuple.

NOT_IN_READING.$comment: [proposal, not in the book; task 3, 92_TASK3_PLAN, chat 21.10 12:50] The record's col equals the value of alias as in no row of the reading named. col and the column behind as must identify the same entity (its identifier, or a column that declares references to it), checked in code. reading is another reading of the same plan that holds no reference itself (depth 1); only under AND from the root of WHERE. Compiled to NOT EXISTS over that reading's own query, entitlement included. An object, not a tuple.

entity.$comment: The table or column the kind refers to, resolved against schema.json. Forbidden with unspecified, required with every other kind. Enforced in code.

missing.$comment: Structured rather than free text. The model names a kind of absence and an entity; the interface renders the sentence from a template. There is no field a cause can be written into.

metric.$comment: A named business measure declared in schema.json, which carries the column expression it compiles to. Where a term has a settled meaning it is declared once as a metric, and the model selects it rather than choosing among columns that could each plausibly express it.

schema.title: Intent Analysis
schema.description: Output of the intent analysis stage of the query assistance pipeline. The model populates a query plan; it does not write a query. The only store reachable is the company SQLite database. Validated before any retrieval is executed (NFR 6, Test 13).

blocked_by: schema.json for the company store. The reference syntax is settled as label.alias, but the schema must state which fields a summary may point at.

The list of mechanical reductions per case type (scope, grouping of identical rows), which depends on the company data structure. Settled: summarization condenses everything it receives and judges no relevance. Reduction before it is mechanical and done in code, items no claim references are recorded in code, and relevance is judged by domain interpretation only.

synthesis.status_note: Written against demo_data/schema.json for the Phase B demo. The book keeps this schema blocked until the company data structure arrives (the fields a reference may resolve to). The approach is in the book: 4.9 states that the answer is drafted with symbolic references resolved into values in code [25]. The exact reference syntax {label.alias#row} is decided here, not in the book.
synthesis.stage: Synthesis, query assistance pipeline (4.9, Table 12). Drafts the answer from the rows retrieved under each reading. Also used for the single redraft after the gate (NFR 19).
post_model_checks: [book NFR 6] Output that does not conform to the schema is rejected.

[book NFR 4, NFR 6] Every sentence carries at least one reference {label.alias#row}. Every reference names a reading that returned rows, an alias in it and a row that exists, and points at a field that is not empty. Code fills each reference from that row, so every value presented is the value in the record.
[book NFR 6] No digit stands outside a reference unless the question holds the same token. A count, a sum or an identifier the model typed is rejected before the gate sees it.

[book NFR 6, NFR 19] Whether the words around the references are true, for example a first place that contradicts the retrieval's ordering, is not decided in code. It is the gate's. Code presents the ordering beside the answer, from the plan's ORDER_BY.
[proposal] Every reading that returned rows carries at least one sentence. Readings that returned no rows carry none: their answer is assembled in code.
[proposal] A rejected output is retried within the model call attempts of Table 15, then the exchange returns request_not_completed.
[book NFR 19, Test 17] Where no assertion survives the gate, after the single redraft, the whole answer is replaced by a request for input, including the records retrieved for it.
notes: The model writes no value. A sentence such as '{late.supplier_id#1} had the most late lines, {late.late_lines#1}.' is filled in code. The answer the gate examines is the filled sentences of a reading, in order.
At most 6 sentences per reading and 3 readings, so at most 18 assertions reach the gate, within 'Assertions examined by the gate' (Table 15, schema 4 maxItems 20).

NFR 21. The conversation history receives the answer with every free-text value (a text column that is neither an identifier nor a closed set of values) left as its reference. Only identifier columns supply the identifiers presented (NFR 27). So text held in a record cannot reach the rewriting call or the identifier check.
A recorded reason (demo: commitments.delay_reason) is quoted as recorded, never stated as the cause. A demo decision, the book does not mention such a field.

schema.title: Synthesis
schema.description: The drafted answer, one entry per reading that returned rows. Sentences carry symbolic references to fields, which code fills.

text.$comment: Text with symbolic references, filled in code: {label.alias#row} for a value in a row, or {label.total} for how many rows the reading matched (D5). At least one of either, as synthesis.check holds; the pattern says the same (G-SENTPAT, chat 21.10, 16:40: it required #row, so a sentence D5 allows was refused).

support_scoring.stage: Gate, query assistance pipeline. A separate model call examining a drafted answer against the material retrieved for it (4.9).
post_model_checks: Every claim.text appears verbatim in the sentence its claim.sentence names, after whitespace normalization. A paraphrase lets a weak assertion be softened and then approved, so a claim not found there rejects the gate output.

[demo extension, 12.10] Every sentence of the answer is named by at least one claim. Output that leaves a sentence uncovered is rejected and the call is retried like any rejected output, so nothing unexamined reaches presentation.
Every reference resolves to an existing reading label and to an alias that was in that reading's SELECT. Otherwise the output is rejected (NFR 6).
supported or contradicted with no reference: rejected.
uncovered with one or more references: rejected.

[12.10] contradicted is treated as unsupported (NFR 19). With symbolic references a contradiction can come only from the words around references, not from a wrong value, so it no longer brings the whole answer down.
Otherwise: assertions verdicted supported are kept, the rest are discarded, and the answer is regenerated once (NFR 19). A sentence is presented only if every claim naming it is supported.
Where no assertion is kept AND the retrieval returned rows, the exchange returns a request for input. An empty retrieval is handled before the gate and is not a failure.
notes: The judge never sees the question. Judging an answer against material and judging it against a question are separate tasks, and the schema has no verdict for irrelevance. Scope is bounded earlier, by what the intent analysis stage placed in SELECT.

Claim decomposition with a small closed set of verdicts is the established pattern for grounding checks where a wrong answer is costly. It is not cited in the book, which presents the gate in 4.9 as examining each assertion against the material retrieved for it without claiming the pattern is standard. The book's basis for rejecting a single numeric score is [39], which measures that self-reported scores concentrate in a narrow high band.
World knowledge does not count as support. This is a prompt constraint, not schema-enforceable.

schema.title: Support Scoring
schema.description: Output of the gate applied before an answer is presented (4.9). The model returns a verdict for each assertion the drafted answer makes, judged only against the material retrieved for it. It returns no score. An assertion the material does not support is removed in code, and the answer is redrafted from those that remain.

claims.$comment: Every assertion the drafted answer makes, in the order it makes them.

sentence.$comment: [demo extension, 12.10] The number of the answer sentence the claim comes from. The gate receives the sentences numbered, so code can check that none was skipped.

text.$comment: The assertion as the answer states it, not a paraphrase. A paraphrase lets a weak assertion be softened and then approved.

verdict.$comment: supported: the retrieved material states it. contradicted: the material states otherwise. uncovered: the material neither states nor denies it. Three categories rather than a number, because 34 measured calls showed a numeric score does not separate sufficient evidence from insufficient, and all 72 outputs fell between 0.65 and 0.95.

evidence.$comment: Required and may be empty. supported and contradicted require at least one entry; uncovered requires none. Enforced in code.

reference.$comment: label.alias, naming a reading from the intent analysis stage and a field of the row it returned. NFR 6.

request_for_input.note: Not a prompt schema. Table 11 lists eight stages and a request for input is not among them, and every trigger for one is already known from the intent analysis output, the retrieval outcome, or the gate verdicts. No model call produces it. It is carried by the exchange response contract below.

exchange_response.stage: Not a pipeline stage. The structure a query assistance exchange returns, assembled in code and rendered by the interface.
assembly_rules: outcome is determined in code from the intent analysis disposition, the retrieval outcome classification, and whether any assertion survived the gate.
checked is rendered from the executed plan by a fixed mapping from clause to phrase. No model writes it.

checked is present on every reading, whether or not the exchange found a gap. A plan that addressed a plausible but wrong column produces no gap and no failed assertion, so exposing it on gap alone would leave the most frequent error class uncovered.
An empty retrieval with no matching rows is outcome answered, not a failure. Emptiness is evidence.
gaps carry no cause. The interface renders each from a template keyed on missing.kind.
missing.entity is required for every kind except unspecified, which must carry none.
Where outcome is referred_to_investigation, readings and gaps are empty and offer_investigation is true.

[demo extension] Each reading carries its records, their total and ordering, assembled in code (query_assistance/contract.py). Where outcome is no_supported_assertion, readings is empty and request_for_input names the readings with what was examined under each (NFR 19 strict reading, Test 17).

templates.no_such_column: {asked}: there is no data. No column in {entity} records it.
templates.no_such_table: {asked}: there is no data. There is no {entity} table.
templates.cross_record_condition: “{asked}” depends on other records of {entity}, which cannot be combined in one question yet. Ask it in two steps: first find them, then ask about them by name.

schema.title: Exchange Response
schema.description: What a query assistance exchange returns. Assembled in code from the intent analysis output, the retrieval outcome, and the gate verdicts. No model call produces it, which is why no field of it can carry a cause (NFR 20).

outcome.$comment: request_not_completed covers a rejected retrieval parameter set (Test 13). It is a system fault, not a request for input, and NFR 20 does not govern it.

readings.$comment: One entry per reading the question carries. FR 11 presents each rather than selecting between them. More than one entry is the multi-reading case of Test 32.

headers.$comment: [demo extension, task 7 review] The name each column is shown by: the label in schema.json, or for an aggregate a phrase built from its expression in code. Never the model's alias, never model text.

identifiers.$comment: [demo extension, task 7 Q3] The columns, in display order, that select an identifier column of schema.json. The interface groups and tags by them; no meaning is read.

title.$comment: [demo extension, task 7 Q2] Built in code: the business description of the one metric the plan names, from schema.json, else 'Reading N'. Never model text.

checked.$comment: What was examined, rendered in code from the executed plan. Never written by a model. This is the only exposure of a plan that addressed a plausible but wrong column, which source [20] places at 29 to 49 percent of model errors and which no gate can detect.

answer.$comment: Prose from the synthesis stage, carrying only assertions the gate found supported. Absent where none survived.

answer_segments.$comment: [demo extension] UI refresh, phase C (chat, 18.10). The answer cut where code filled a reference: joined, the segments are the answer exactly. A segment with ref names the alias and the 1-based row of this reading's rows it was filled from, so the screen can point at the row. A value from a free-text column carries no ref (NFR 21). Built in code (synthesis.Draft.segments), never by a model.

result.$comment: [demo extension] The retrieval outcome classification, in code (Test 35). name_ambiguous and name_not_matched: chat 20.10, a name the user wrote matched several entities or none [proposal, not in the book].

candidates.$comment: [demo extension] Chat 20.10, V5: on name_ambiguous only, for each name that matched several entities, up to max_candidates of them as 'name (identifier)' and how many more, counted within the user's entitlement. For the screen only: never in a prompt, the history, the presented identifiers or the exchange record.

columns.$comment: [demo extension] The SELECT aliases, in order.

rows.$comment: [demo extension] The records retrieved, as returned. Presented by code, not by a model (NFR 6).

total.$comment: [demo extension] Rows the query matches before LIMIT. Shown as 'N of total' where it exceeds row_count.

entity.$comment: [demo extension, long list L4] The schema.json label of the FROM table, sent only where each row is a row of it: plain columns, no GROUP_BY, every JOIN many-to-one by declared keys (references); or (D10) grouped by exactly one identifier column, naming the table it identifies. Built in code from the catalog, never model text.

ordered_by.$comment: [demo extension] Rendered from ORDER_BY. Lets the person see which row is first, which code cannot verify in the wording (synthesis).

not_held.$comment: [demo extension] Identifiers the existence check did not find, and where it looked (4.9).

notice.$comment: [demo extension] A fixed sentence from code: no match, not held, or N of total.

text.$comment: [demo extension] The template filled in code.

offer_investigation.$comment: FR 14. Carries no cause, plausible or otherwise (Test 22).

understood_as.$comment: FR 25. The rewritten question, present only where the conversation had earlier exchanges. Copied in code from the rewriting stage, never written by the synthesis model.

notice.$comment: [demo extension] A fixed sentence from code for referral, unreachable source or request not completed.

withheld.$comment: [demo extension, 12.10] A fixed sentence from code, present where the gate removed a statement and something remains. Never says what was removed.

unanswered_parts.$comment: [proposal, not in the book] Task 4 (91_COVERAGE_PLAN): a part of the question no reading answered. text is the model's sentence with code's slots filled, where it passed coverage.message(), else contract.UNANSWERED. ask shows the person's own words; follow_up is what a click sends, where coverage.follow_up() accepted it, else the part as written. Task 3 (chat 21.10, 12:50): a part the plan language cannot express carries code's reason (coverage.REASONS, not_expressible) and, where asking it on its own would meet the same limit, no ask and no follow_up.

referred_parts.$comment: [proposal, not in the book] Task 4, C: a part of the question that asks for a cause, a judgement or an action. Its readings are not answered; show_recorded names the readings whose records a click shows, by the plan kept on the server, with no model call.

replaced.$comment: [proposal, not in the book] Task 4, B: a fixed sentence from code, present where a sentence that presented a recorded value as a cause was replaced by the value as recorded, or removed.

coverage_notice.$comment: [proposal, not in the book] Task 4: a fixed sentence from code, present where C or B could not be completed (GAP-07 in task 4's scope).

ambiguous_terms.$comment: [demo extension, task 7 Q4] The terms intent analysis declared ambiguous (ambiguous[].term), only those that are a span of the question as posed. Lets the interface say which term was read in more than one way. Present only on answered with more than one reading.

request_for_input.$comment: [demo extension] NFR 19 strict reading, NFR 20: where no assertion survives, the answer and its records are replaced by this. It names the readings under which the question was taken, and no cause.

question_rewriting.stage: Question rewriting, query assistance pipeline only. Runs where the conversation has earlier exchanges (4.9, Table 12).
post_model_checks: question is non-empty after trimming.
Where carried_from_history is false, question equals the question as posed after whitespace normalization. A rewrite that claims to carry nothing and still changes the question is rejected.

The rewritten question is presented with the answer (FR 25) and recorded. It is never a source of identifiers (NFR 27): the compiler checks identifiers against the question as posed, earlier exchanges and presented identifiers only.

schema.title: Question Rewriting
schema.description: Output of the rewriting stage. The current question restated so that it stands on its own, in the language it was posed in. It does not answer the question.

carried_from_history.$comment: false where the question already stands on its own or changes topic. Recorded, and lets the measurement in phase B separate rewrites from pass-throughs.

question_classification.stage: [proposal, not in the book] Task 4, C: what each part of the question asks, from the question alone. Runs on every question that retrieves, beside retrieval and synthesis (91_COVERAGE_PLAN, chat 20.10).
post_model_checks: Every asked is a span of the question as posed, or of the rewritten question (compiler._check_span).

A part that asks for a cause or a judgement and overlaps a reading's asked takes that reading's sentences away from the answer: the part is referred to an investigation (coverage.apply_classification).

schema.title: Question Classification
schema.description: What each part of the question asks. It sees the question only: no plan, no record, no answer.

asked.$comment: A span of the question, verified in code.

asks.$comment: recorded: values the records hold, a recorded reason among them. cause: why something happened. judgement: whether a value is unusual or acceptable. action: a change to the records or anything to be done.

coverage_check.stage: [proposal, not in the book] Task 4, B: after the last gate, whether each part of the question was answered, and how each sentence relates values. Skipped only under S1 to S4 (coverage.COVERAGE_SKIP). Sees no record: the sentences as references, the parts, what each reading examined.
post_model_checks: Every part sent is in the output once, in order, by its asked; every sentence number once.

A message is shown only where its slots resolve, {part} and {reason} once each, and it holds no digit, no identifier, no catalog name, no causal word and no negation outside {reason} (chat 22:40, 22:50); else the fixed template.
A follow_up is sent only where every identifier in it is in the conversation (NFR 27), it holds no digit the question does not, and it ends with a question mark; else the part as written.

schema.title: Coverage Check
schema.description: Per part of the question: answered, declared or not answered. Per sentence: a kind after Yu et al. (EMNLP 2019).

message.$comment: not_answered only: one sentence with {part} and {reason}, which code fills.

follow_up.$comment: not_answered only: the part as a question that stands on its own.

schema.json.purpose: The queryable surface. Entities with their columns and types, metrics that name a business term and the column expression it compiles to, and the entitlement rule per role. What is not here does not exist as far as the model is concerned. Declaring a term as a metric turns schema linking from a guess into a lookup, which is the cheapest of the three defences against a plan that is valid but addresses the wrong column.
blocked_by: Company SQLite inventory: tables, columns, types.
The terms the client uses and what each means in the data. A term without a settled meaning is not declared as a metric and falls to the other two defences.

relations.json.purpose: Declared relations for JOIN. Each relation names its column pairs in full so a composite key cannot be joined on one column.

retrieval_outcome_classification.$comment: Determined in code after retrieval, before the gate. Four outcomes, only the third of which the judge sees. An identifier is a column marked identifier in schema.json, compared with EQ or IN at the top level of WHERE or under AND. Under OR it does not restrict the result and is not checked. The check replaces an earlier design that re-ran the plan without its identity predicate, which reported a held identifier as absent whenever other rows met the remaining conditions. Checking where the identifier is held, rather than in the filtered column, replaces a later one that reported a supplier with no lines as absent.

outcomes.name: not_plannable
outcomes.when: The intent analysis stage could not map part of the question to a plan.
outcomes.known: Before retrieval, from the unresolved field of schema 1.
outcomes.response: Name what was asked and the table, column, or absent source that would allow it to be retrieved.

outcomes.name: empty_no_match
outcomes.when: The plan ran and returned no rows, and every identifier the plan names is held. An identifier is checked where it is held: the column its schema.json entry declares under references (commitments.supplier_id is held in suppliers.supplier_id), or its own column where none is declared or the user may not read the referenced table.
outcomes.known: In code, one existence check per identifier the plan names, within the user's entitlement. No model call.
outcomes.response: A valid answer. Nothing matched. This is evidence, not a failure.

outcomes.name: empty_unknown_entity
outcomes.when: The plan returned no rows, and an identifier the plan names is not held, checked as above.
outcomes.known: In code, same existence checks. The response names each identifier not held.
outcomes.response: The identifier the question named is not present in the data.

outcomes.name: rows_returned
outcomes.response: Proceed to synthesis and then to the gate. This is the only outcome the gate applies to.

outcomes.name: name_ambiguous
outcomes.when: A name the plan matches (MATCHES) is held by several entities the user may see, counted by the entity's own identifier.
outcomes.known: In code, before retrieval: three stages (equal ignoring case, starts with, contains), within the user's entitlement. No model call.
outcomes.response: Nothing is retrieved. A fixed request to ask again with the full name; the candidates are shown on the screen only. [proposal, not in the book; chat 20.10]

outcomes.name: name_not_matched
outcomes.when: A name the plan matches (MATCHES) is held by no entity the user may see.
outcomes.response: Nothing is retrieved. A valid answer: no record carries that name. [proposal, not in the book; chat 20.10]

unreachable.$comment: A fifth situation exists and cannot be detected. The plan is valid, rows are returned, and every assertion is genuinely supported by them, but the plan addressed the wrong table or filtered on the wrong column, so the answer is grounded in the wrong material. No gate can find this, because the gate checks an answer against its material and the material is what is wrong. The response is exposure rather than detection: FR 11 requires every reading to be shown, so the person sees what was retrieved and judges it. Source [20] places schema linking at 29 to 49 percent of model errors, which makes this the most frequent failure, not an edge case. It is stated as a problem in section 8.1 of the book.

wrong_column_defences.$comment: A plan can be valid, execute, return real rows, and have every assertion supported by them, while addressing a column that is not the one the question meant. No gate detects this, because the gate checks an answer against its material and the material is what is wrong. Source [20] places schema linking at 29 to 49 percent of model errors. Three defences apply, none of which is a guarantee, and they compose.

defences.name: declared metrics
defences.catches: Terms whose meaning was settled in advance.
defences.misses: A term nobody thought to declare.

defences.name: declared ambiguity
defences.catches: Terms the model itself recognized as open.
defences.misses: A term the model was confident and wrong about.

defences.name: exposure
defences.catches: Everything, since the executed plan is always rendered.
defences.misses: Whatever the person does not read.

rejected.name: execution-guided self-consistency
rejected.reason: Sampling k plans and treating disagreement as ambiguity reduces schema linking errors, but the benefit shrinks as the base model improves, and a model that is consistently wrong passes it unchanged. It measures confidence, not correctness. It also costs k times the calls on every question, and [39] measures sampling five times as 38 percent worse calibrated than asking the model once, so the cost buys less than a single call already provides.

rejected.name: conformal prediction over hidden layers
rejected.reason: Requires access to the model's internal layers. The system reaches a model endpoint through a unified client and has none.

placeholders_comment: Working values, not decided. Section 5.3 of the book states what each is derived from without fixing a number, and every value here is replaced at deployment.
